claims.claim_text: Orexis is the moved mover, characterized as 'that which at once moves and is moved' (433b17-18).
The realizable good is the unmoved originator that draws the desiring soul without being drawn in turn (433b10-18).
The animal via the bodily instrument — the ball-and-socket joint where 'pushing and pulling' execute the action (433b21-25) — is that which is moved.

The schema is preserved across all three types of action because it specifies the fundamental kinetic structure of any orectic actualization, not the contingent character of any particular such actualization.

claims.claim_text: In the case of technē (craft), where the ergon (work, product) is decisive, 'training has the precise sense of reducing deliberation insofar as it is through training that the completedness of attaining a result comes about' (GA 18, p. 127); cultivated hexis fires as routine.

In the case of praxis (action) and aretē (virtue, excellence), 'the how is only appropriated in such a way that the human being enables himself to be composed at each moment; not routine but holding-oneself-open' (GA 18, p. 128).

Aristotle indicates that the affective force of doxa-mediated desire is both immediate (euthus, DA III.3, 427b23) and involuntary: 'it is not in our power to form opinions as we will' (427b20).

claims.claim_text: The chain runs through doxa into pathē into action with the same continuity that the simpler chains exhibit, but the orexis that emerges into bodily motion is no longer generic appetite — it is the determinate desire structured by the cognitive-conative-hedonic-physiological composite the pathos names.

The kinetic roles for Type 3: unmoved originator is the realizable good as articulated under the evaluative category (just retaliation, saved life, relief of undeserved suffering); moved mover is the emotion-desire composite (anger-as-desire-to-retaliate, fear-as-desire-to-flee, pity-as-desire-to-relieve); animal-via-bodily-instrument is moved with the somatic preparation specific to the emotion's eidetic structure.
In Type 3, hexeis operate in a register distinct from their Type 2 role.

claims.claim_text: Where Type 2 hexis is technē-hexis (settled doxa furnishing the universal premise of the practical syllogism, fired routinely), Type 3 hexeis are praxis-hexeis: sedimented dispositions of emotional comportment, the diachronic residue of repeated pathos-actualizations (cf. §1.7), cultivated as the standing capacity for rightly-disposed comportment toward the pathē the situation demands.

The Aristotelian texts confirm the bivalent character: hexis qua dynamis is both active power and passive power (Met. Δ 12, 1019a 15 ff.); the same settled capacity exercised as praxis is what is struck or displaced in pathos.

claims.claim_text: Courage is the praxis-hexis of fear; magnanimity the praxis-hexis of anger; modesty the praxis-hexis of shame; aretē more generally is the cultivated hexis that fits the kairos, the right disposition before the right matter at the right moment, defined as Aristotle has it by 'the phronimos as the prudent one would define it' (NE B 6, 1106b 36).

claims.claim_text: The praxis-hexis structure of virtuous action explains why courage is not the absence of fear but the cultivated comportment-toward-fear: the brave person fears the genuinely fearsome (NE III.7, 1115b 7-13), and what aretē cultivates is the how of the fearing — fearing rightly, in the right manner, at the right moment, before the right matter.

claims.claim_text: These hexeis modulate Type 3 chains in two distinct ways: (1) they modulate the input to doxa (perceptual-affective biasing); (2) they modulate the gating of doxa into pathē (which pathē arise, at what evaluative threshold, with what intensity).
claims.interpretive_flag_recommended: The two-modulation thesis is dissertation-novel architectural elaboration; flag substantially.

claims.claim_text: The cowardly person sees enemies in shadows where the courageous person sees only shadows; the basic-valence channel has already been re-saturated by prior fear-actualizations.
The perceptual encounter is conducted under the resulting Stimmung-shading (cf. §1.7's diachronic analysis).

The courageous person's doxa-gate produces a regulated, action-prepared fear rather than a paralyzed fear; the irascible person's doxa-gate fires anger more readily on thinner evaluative content; the modest person's gate produces shame on circumstances the shameless person's gate ignores entirely.

claims.claim_text: The Rhetoric II analyses presuppose this hexis-modulation throughout: Aristotle's diagnostic categories specify 'those of such-and-such a character feel anger toward such-and-such persons,' which is a description of hexis-conditioning of the doxa-gate.

claims.claim_text: The structural distinction matters: Type 2 hexis operates at the doxa level (settled doxai enabling rapid practical inference); Type 3 hexeis operate at both the basic-valence level (perceptual-affective biasing) and the doxa-gate level (which pathē arise and with what intensity). The same Aristotelian term names two structurally distinct dispositional functions.
claims.interpretive_flag_recommended: Per Special Instruction (f) — confirm consistency with §1.4's hexis-bivalence treatment. The two-level operation (basic-valence + doxa-gate) for Type 3 is a substantial architectural elaboration; flag.

claims.claim_text: The recognition of the distinction is what enables the chain-apparatus to handle both rationally articulated craft-action and emotionally complex situational action without collapsing the two into a single dispositional model.
Phantasia, phantasma, doxa, and pathē together articulate every action the chain produces.
Aristotle defines phantasia as 'a movement resulting from actual perception' (DA III.3, 429a1-2).

Phantasia operates in all three action types, but differently in each: as the immediate phantasma identifying the present object in Type 1; as the settled phantasma informing the universal premise of the practical syllogism in Type 2; and as the projected phantasma over which doxa operates in Type 3.
claims.interpretive_flag_recommended: The tri-modal-phantasia thesis is a significant user architectural move; flag

claims.claim_text: 'Both the man who remembers and the man who hopes,' Aristotle observes, 'will be attended by an imagination of what he remembers or hopes' (Rhetoric I.11, 1370a28-30).
The temporal depth of emotional life is supplied by phantasia, and the feared evil that does not yet exist is given to the soul as phantasma, the soul moving as though the feared thing were present.
The phantasma is what doxa operates upon; what doxa ratifies as true is the phantasma's taking-as.
claims.interpretive_flag_recommended: 'Taking-as' is Heideggerian; flag attribution. The phantasma-as-substrate-doxa-as-ratifier architecture is interpretive.

claims.claim_text: The doxa-gate is content-conditional across all three types: absent in Type 1, present-but-non-evaluative in Type 2, present-and-evaluative in Type 3.
Emotion enters the chain wherever the appearance discloses evaluatively complex content that doxa ratifies as true, and it enters as the form desire takes under that disclosure.
What phantasia presents, doxa commits to; what doxa commits to, emotion mobilizes; what emotion mobilizes, action completes.
claims.interpretive_flag_recommended: This four-part climactic gradatio is the section's most rhetorically marked sentence and one of the chapter's strongest. Mark it as the user's interpretive synthesis (it is not in Aristotle or Heidegger directly).

remediation.rationale: The sentence's rhetorical force should be preserved; flagging via footnote rather than inline marker.

claims.claim_text: The chain closes at A_4 but does not stop.

The completed action transforms the perceptual environment, producing new sensible conditions that serve as A_0 for a new cycle. The chain is recursive, not linear: A_4 produces A_0', and the cycle resumes with the world now altered by the action that closed the prior cycle.
claims.interpretive_flag_recommended: The recursivity thesis is dissertation-novel architectural elaboration not directly in Aristotle. Flag.

claims.claim_text: This recursivity is what makes the chain a chain rather than a sequence, and it is what makes the analysis of action a generative apparatus rather than a one-pass diagnostic.

The recursive structure secures Heidegger's reading of hexis as the determination of the genuineness of being-there in a moment of being-composed: each pass through the chain re-cultivates the dispositional ground, and the cumulative trajectory of the agent's chain-actualizations IS their hexis-formation.

claims.claim_text: The threefold structure of the pathē that Aristotle isolates in Rhetoric B 1, 1378a 24 — 'how we find ourselves, what we are attuned to, with respect to whom' — is, on Heidegger's reading, the proto-form of what Being and Time §29 will name Befindlichkeit (state-of-mind, 'finding-oneself,' attunement).
